decision: Which upgrade prompt and funnel stage is losing the most paid upgrades, and are the differences between prompts real?
limitations: Prompts reach different users at different moments, so the fix-first gain ranks where to look, not what a change will add. Test the fix with an A/B test.
It holds no benchmarks and only compares your prompts with each other. With small counts the corrected tests will often say prompts are not distinguishable yet.
Counts must be unique users, one period and one attribution rule. View-through upgrades are left out, and mixed units make every rate wrong.
It cannot see what happens after the upgrade. A prompt that lifts conversion while upgraded users churn is overselling; check retention separately.
review: The product or growth lead confirms the four event counts are unique users for one period, tagged by prompt, and that no limit gates the activation path, before a prompt is rewritten or moved.
